info.title: Reliable Checkout and Customer Rewards API
info.description:
Use **Try it out** and **Execute** below to call this running service. No API client installation or credentials are needed.

### Quick walkthrough
1. Create a customer and copy its returned id.
2. List products; the seeded Notebook ID is already provided as an item-path example.
3. Create a cart with your real customer ID and copy its returned id.
4. Add an item using PUT and your real cart ID.
5. Checkout with a unique Idempotency-Key and the default empty body.
6. Execute the identical checkout again to verify durable replay, then retrieve its order.
7. Inspect customer coupons and the admin report. Use an owned coupon code on a later cart to redeem it.

Example UUIDs are placeholders: replace customer/cart/order IDs with values returned by your requests. Use a new checkout key for each new cart, retaining the same key and coupon on retries.

Milestones use the environment policy, default n=5 and x=10. Every fifth store-wide order automatically earns a customer-specific coupon. Admin generation normally returns 409 because it only repairs missing historical rewards.

Prices are exact decimal INR strings. Carts use live prices without reservations. Orders are immutable snapshots. Authentication is out of scope: customer IDs are trusted inputs and Administration operations are administrative.

post.summary: Checkout a cart with optional coupon
post.description: Use a unique key for this customer/cart. Same key, cart and coupon replay the original successful response even after restart. Changed cart/coupon inputs conflict. Failed attempts leave the key reusable. Inventory, order, redemption, reward and replay storage commit together or all roll back. A coupon is usable only by its owner and cannot discount its earning order.

get.summary: View reconciled revenue and reward report
get.description: Read-only consistent snapshot. Revenue derives from immutable orders, quantities from order items, and coupon counts reconcile with records. Includes zero-purchase products; labels are current catalog names. No pagination.
